You must be able to answer: What are input, processing, output, syntax, runtime and logic errors?
You are ready to move on when…: You can trace a 5-line program and explain its output.

You must be able to answer: What changes when x=x+1? What is a variable's current value?
You are ready to move on when…: You can trace variable updates line by line.

You must be able to answer: Difference between 5, 5.0, '5', True; when do conversions fail?
You are ready to move on when…: You can predict types and avoid accidental string concatenation.
You can evaluate expressions manually and use parentheses clearly.

You must be able to answer: How do I read input and print exactly what the prompt requests?
You are ready to move on when…: You can solve tiny input/output exercises with correct format.

You must be able to answer: How do if/elif/else and nested conditions execute?
You are ready to move on when…: You pass boundary tests for ranges and classifications.

You must be able to answer: How many iterations run? What changes each iteration?
You are ready to move on when…: You can trace for/while loops and prove termination.

You must be able to answer: When should initial value be 0, 1, first item or None?
You are ready to move on when…: You can calculate sum, count, product, min and max correctly.

You must be able to answer: Parameters vs arguments? Return vs print? Local vs global?
You are ready to move on when…: You can write reusable functions and test return values.
Common trap: Everything placed in one giant function.

You must be able to answer: List/array, tuple, set, dictionary/map: when and why?
You are ready to move on when…: You can choose a collection and explain its trade-off.
Common trap: Using a set when order matters.

You must be able to answer: What is an index? How do slicing, mutability and normalization work?
You are ready to move on when…: You handle empty, one-character, repeated and whitespace cases.

You must be able to answer: How do I turn English into steps and pseudocode?
You are ready to move on when…: You can write a plan before syntax for 5 problems.

You must be able to answer: How do I isolate an error and choose edge cases?
You are ready to move on when…: Every solution has normal, boundary and invalid/no-answer tests.

You must be able to answer: How do work and memory grow as input grows?
You are ready to move on when…: You can justify common Big-O classifications.

You must be able to answer: When do I use hashing, two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums, binary search?
You are ready to move on when…: You can explain why the pattern fits constraints.
Common trap: Forcing a memorized pattern onto every problem.

You must be able to answer: How do stacks, queues, linked lists, trees and graphs behave?
You are ready to move on when…: You can implement basic operations and state complexity.

You must be able to answer: How do queries, joins, grouping, transactions, processes and networking work?
You are ready to move on when…: You can answer verbally and solve basic exercises.

You must be able to answer: How do I clarify, propose brute force, optimize, test and explain?
You are ready to move on when…: You can solve and communicate a problem in a timed mock.
